indicators.name: us_2y
indicators.label: US 2Y Treasury
indicators.notes: US 2-Year Treasury yield. Reflects market expectations of the Fed funds rate over the next 2 years; the front-end anchor and a key driver of curve shape.

indicators.name: us_10y
indicators.label: US 10Y Treasury
indicators.notes: US 10-Year Treasury yield. The global risk-free benchmark; anchors mortgages, corporate borrowing costs, and cross-border rate markets.

indicators.name: us_30y
indicators.label: US 30Y Treasury
indicators.notes: US 30-Year Treasury bond yield (the long bond). Most sensitive to inflation expectations, fiscal sustainability concerns, and structural demand from long-duration buyers (insurers, pensions, foreign reserve managers).

indicators.name: us_10y_term_premium
indicators.label: US 10Y term premium (ACM)
indicators.notes: Adrian-Crump-Moench (ACM) model term premium on the 10Y, published by NY Fed. The compensation investors demand for holding long-duration risk beyond what expected short-rate paths can justify. Rising values indicate structural repricing of sovereign duration — often driven by fiscal concerns or weakening foreign demand.

indicators.name: sofr
indicators.label: SOFR
indicators.notes: Secured Overnight Financing Rate. The post-LIBOR USD benchmark; reflects the true cost of overnight Treasury repo. Spikes (relative to IORB) flag dollar funding stress, as in the September 2019 repo blowup.

indicators.name: iorb
indicators.label: IORB
indicators.notes: Interest on Reserve Balances. Rate the Fed pays banks on excess reserves; the de facto floor of the fed funds corridor and benchmark for SOFR.

indicators.name: rrp_usage
indicators.label: ON RRP usage
indicators.notes: Overnight Reverse Repo Program take-up. Money-market funds park cash with the Fed when private-market yields are unattractive. A draining RRP signals cash flowing back into private repo and T-Bills; a swelling RRP signals excess liquidity with nowhere to go.

indicators.name: tga_balance
indicators.label: Treasury TGA balance
indicators.notes: Treasury General Account balance at the Fed. The US Treasury's checking account. Drawdowns inject liquidity into the banking system; refills (e.g. post debt-ceiling deals) drain it. Key variable around X-date risk windows.

indicators.name: fed_balance_sheet
indicators.label: Fed total assets (H.4.1)
indicators.notes: Total assets on the Fed's weekly H.4.1 balance sheet. Tracks QE expansion and QT runoff; the broadest single gauge of central bank liquidity supply.

indicators.name: ig_oas
indicators.label: US IG corporate OAS
indicators.notes: ICE BofA US Investment-Grade Corporate Index option-adjusted spread over Treasuries. The compensation for IG credit + liquidity risk. Widening signals rising default expectations and/or deteriorating bank balance sheets.

indicators.name: hy_oas
indicators.label: US HY corporate OAS
indicators.notes: ICE BofA US High-Yield Corporate Index OAS. The 'risk gauge' of corporate credit. HY spreads typically lead equity drawdowns by days to weeks and are the cleanest read on leverage-system stress.

indicators.name: usdjpy
indicators.label: USD/JPY
indicators.notes: USD/JPY spot. Captures the Fed-BOJ policy gap and the temperature of yen carry-trade positioning. A sharp drop (yen strength) signals carry-unwind and tends to precede global risk-off (e.g. Aug 2024).

indicators.name: gbpusd
indicators.label: GBP/USD
indicators.notes: GBP/USD spot. Key gauge of UK fiscal/political credibility; LDI-style stress (Sep 2022) typically shows here first as foreign holders dump gilts and convert proceeds back to home currency.

indicators.name: dxy
indicators.label: DXY US Dollar Index
indicators.notes: ICE US Dollar Index. Trade-weighted USD vs a basket of major currencies. A rising DXY tightens global dollar liquidity and pressures EM/commodity complexes.

indicators.name: vix
indicators.label: VIX (equity vol)
indicators.notes: CBOE Volatility Index. 30-day implied vol on S&P 500 options — the 'equity fear gauge'. Sustained levels above 25 = elevated risk; spikes above 40 historically coincide with macro shocks.

indicators.name: move
indicators.label: MOVE (Treasury vol)
indicators.notes: Merrill Option Volatility Estimate. The Treasury-market equivalent of VIX: implied vol weighted across 2/5/10/30Y options. The single most important rates-market stress gauge — spikes in MOVE precede most US fixed-income dislocations (LDI 2022, SVB 2023, basis-trade unwinds).

indicators.name: kre
indicators.label: KRE (regional banks)
indicators.notes: SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF. Most direct read on US regional bank stress — this cohort holds the largest unrealised losses on HTM Treasuries and is most exposed to a duration shock (SVB-style risk).

indicators.name: nikkei
indicators.label: Nikkei 225
indicators.notes: Nikkei 225 Index. Tokyo's price-weighted blue-chip index; export-heavy composition makes it highly sensitive to USD/JPY and global growth. Sharp drops often signal carry-unwind underway (e.g. -12% on 5 Aug 2024).

indicators.name: topix_banks
indicators.label: TOPIX Banks (1615.T)
indicators.notes: TOPIX Banks sector ETF. Japanese bank stocks reflect JGB capital pressure via NIM expansion (positive) and HTM unrealised losses (negative); a useful barometer of how Japanese banks are processing rising long-end yields.

indicators.name: ftse100
indicators.label: FTSE 100
indicators.notes: FTSE 100 Index. UK blue chips dominated by global commodity, financial, and pharma names; less reflective of UK domestic stress than FTSE 250.

indicators.name: gold
indicators.label: Gold (CME front)
indicators.notes: Gold front-month futures (COMEX). Classic hedge against sovereign credit risk, inflation, and currency debasement. Rising despite stable real rates is a clean signal of structural sovereign-risk repricing.

indicators.name: btc
indicators.label: Bitcoin
indicators.notes: Bitcoin spot (USD). Alternative store-of-value; correlation regime shifts — at times tracks risk assets, at times tracks gold. Useful as a tail-hedge indicator when traditional safe havens are also under stress.

indicators.name: tlt
indicators.label: TLT (US 20+Y bonds)
indicators.notes: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF. Proxy for long-duration Treasury total return. Falling TLT = long-end yields rising; large drawdowns confirm structural repricing in the long bond.

indicators.name: uk_gilt_etf
indicators.label: IGLT.L (UK gilts ETF)
indicators.notes: iShares Core UK Gilts UCITS ETF. Price-based UK gilt stress proxy used when direct gilt-yield feeds are unavailable. ETF duration is ~14 years, so each 1% price drop corresponds to roughly a 7-8 bp yield rise across the curve. Used in lieu of UK 30Y yield in the composite stress index.

indicators.name: jgb_10y
indicators.label: JGB 10Y
indicators.notes: Japan 10-Year Government Bond yield. Long the BOJ's YCC target — rising values signal monetary normalisation, JGB demand erosion, and broader global liquidity tightening as Japanese institutions repatriate.

indicators.name: jgb_30y
indicators.label: JGB 30Y
indicators.notes: Japan 30-Year JGB yield. Highly sensitive to BOJ purchase pace and life-insurance ALM demand. The single most important non-US sovereign-rate signal: a 25 bp move here translates into hundreds of billions of USD of potential reallocation flow globally.

indicators.name: jgb_40y
indicators.label: JGB 40Y
indicators.notes: Japan 40-Year JGB yield. The longest tenor JGB issued; lowest liquidity, most volatile, often leads the JGB curve. Levels above 3% are historically rare and stress thin pension/insurance demand.
